input: Given /data/team_a.txt and /data/team_b.txt containing member names (one per line, already sorted), use the comm command to find: 1) Members only in Team A (print under 'Only Team A:'). 2) Members only in Team B (print under 'Only Team B:'). 3) Members in both teams (print under 'Both teams:'). Print the count of each group.

transcript.final_response:
```text
Only Team A:
alice
dave
eve
Count: 3

Only Team B:
frank
grace
Count: 2

Both teams:
bob
carol
Count: 2
```
tool_calls:
a_only=$(comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)
b_only=$(comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)
both=$(comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt)
printf 'Only Team A:\n'
comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
printf 'Count: %s\n\n' "$(comm -23 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"
printf 'Only Team B:\n'
comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
printf 'Count: %s\n\n' "$(comm -13 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"
printf 'Both teams:\n'
comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt
printf 'Count: %s\n' "$(comm -12 /data/team_a.txt /data/team_b.txt | wc -l)"
